articles.title: Towards the Representation of Genomic Data in HL7 FHIR and OMOP CDM
articles.journal: Studies in health technology and informatics

knowledge.research_objective: Create semantic mapping from raw genomic data to both FHIR and OMOP CDM and analyze the data coverage of both models.
healthcare_standards: OMOP CDM (Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model)
knowledge.etl_architecture: An ETL pipeline that maps raw genomic VCF files to FHIR as an intermediate representation and then transforms the FHIR data into OMOP CDM format.
mapping_techniques: calculation of mapping scores for different data categories
evaluation_methods: calculated mapping score for different data categories
measured relative data coverage in both FHIR and OMOP CDM
main_findings: Patient genomic data can be mapped directly to OMOP CDM from VCF files with a coverage slightly over 50%.
Using FHIR as an intermediate representation does not cause additional information loss; transformation from FHIR to OMOP CDM achieves almost 100% success.
Extending OMOP CDM with patient genomic data via ETL enables researchers to apply various analysis methods, including machine learning.
knowledge.future_directions: Extend OMOP CDM with patient genomic data using ETL to support advanced analyses such as machine learning algorithms.

supporting_evidence.claim: Semantic mapping from raw genomic data to both FHIR and OMOP CDM was created and data coverage analyzed.
supporting_evidence.quote: we have created semantic mapping from raw genomic data to both FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) and OMOP (Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership) CDM (Common Data Model) and analyzed the data coverage of both models.

supporting_evidence.claim: Mapping scores and relative data coverage were calculated for different data categories.
supporting_evidence.quote: we calculated the mapping score for different data categories and the relative data coverage in both FHIR and OMOP CDM.

supporting_evidence.claim: Direct mapping of patient genomic data to OMOP CDM from VCF files achieves slightly over 50% coverage.
supporting_evidence.quote: Our results show, that the patients genomic data can be mapped to OMOP CDM directly from VCF (Variant Call Format) file with a coverage of slightly over 50%.

supporting_evidence.claim: Using FHIR as an intermediate representation results in almost 100% successful transformation to OMOP CDM.
supporting_evidence.quote: However, using FHIR as intermediate representation does not lead to further information loss as the already stored data in FHIR can be further transformed into OMOP CDM format with almost 100% success.

supporting_evidence.claim: Extending OMOP CDM with patient genomic data via ETL enables application of machine learning algorithms.
supporting_evidence.quote: Our findings are in favor of extending OMOP CDM with patient genomic data using ETL to enable the researchers to apply different analysis methods including machine learning algorithms on genomic data.

articles.title: FHIR-Ontop-OMOP: Building clinical knowledge graphs in FHIR RDF with the OMOP Common data Model

knowledge.research_objective: To develop and evaluate methods and tools that expose the OMOP CDM-based clinical data repositories into virtual clinical KGs that are compliant with FHIR Resource Description Framework (RDF) specification.
knowledge.etl_architecture: The FHIR-Ontop-OMOP system generates virtual clinical knowledge graphs from OMOP relational databases by using Ontop to map OMOP tables to FHIR RDF resources.
evaluation_methods: Comparison of patient counts obtained via SQL queries on the MIMIC database and SPARQL queries on the virtual KG to assess transformation faithfulness
Validation that RDF triples for 100 patients conform to the FHIR RDF specification
main_findings: A beta version of the FHIR-Ontop-OMOP system was released.
Implemented more than 100 data element mappings from 11 OMOP CDM tables covering 11 FHIR resources.

The generated virtual KG from MIMIC-III contains tens of millions of FHIR resource instances (e.g., 46,520 Patients, 716,595 Conditions, 1,063,525 Procedures, 24,934,751 MedicationStatements, 365,181,104 Observations, 4,779,672 CodeableConcepts).
Patient counts from five pairs of SQL and SPARQL queries were identical, confirming faithful data transformation.
RDF triples for 100 patients were fully conformant with the FHIR RDF specification.

supporting_evidence.claim: Research objective is to develop and evaluate methods and tools that expose OMOP CDM repositories as virtual clinical KGs compliant with FHIR RDF.
supporting_evidence.quote: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate methods and tools that expose the OMOP CDM-based clinical data repositories into virtual clinical KGs that are compliant with FHIR Resource Description Framework (RDF) specification.

supporting_evidence.claim: The study leverages community-based standards FHIR and OMOP CDM.
supporting_evidence.quote: From the standardization perspective, community-based standards such as the Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) and the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model (CDM) are increasingly used to represent and standardize EHR data for clinical data analytics

supporting_evidence.claim: System architecture generates virtual clinical KGs from OMOP relational databases using Ontop.
supporting_evidence.quote: We developed a system called FHIR-Ontop-OMOP to generate virtual clinical KGs from the OMOP relational databases.

supporting_evidence.claim: The system was evaluated using an OMOP CDM‑based MIMIC‑III data repository.
supporting_evidence.quote: We leveraged an OMOP CDM-based Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care (MIMIC-III) data repository to evaluate the FHIR-Ontop-OMOP system

supporting_evidence.claim: More than 100 data element mappings covering 11 FHIR resources were implemented.
supporting_evidence.quote: A total of more than 100 data element mappings from 11 OMOP CDM clinical data, health system and vocabulary tables were implemented in the system, covering 11 FHIR resources.

supporting_evidence.claim: Patient counts from SQL and SPARQL queries were identical, ensuring faithful transformation.
supporting_evidence.quote: Patient counts identified by five pairs of SQL (over the MIMIC database) and SPARQL (over the virtual CKG) queries were identical, ensuring the faithfulness of the data transformation.

supporting_evidence.claim: RDF triples for 100 patients were fully conformant with the FHIR RDF specification.
supporting_evidence.quote: Generated CKG in RDF triples for 100 patients were fully conformant with the FHIR RDF specification.

supporting_evidence.claim: The generated virtual KG contains large numbers of FHIR resource instances.
supporting_evidence.quote: The generated virtual CKG from MIMIC-III contains 46,520 instances of FHIR Patient, 716,595 instances of Condition, 1,063,525 instances of Procedure, 24,934,751 instances of MedicationStatement, 365,181,104 instances of Observations, and 4,779,672 instances of CodeableConcept.

articles.title: From OpenEHR to FHIR and OMOP Data Model for Microbiology Findings.
articles.journal: Studies in health technology and informatics

knowledge.research_objective: To map infection control related data from openEHR to FHIR and subsequently to OMOP CDM to enable interoperability and support research.
main_findings: Mapping across three standards (openEHR, FHIR, OMOP CDM) was successfully performed, establishing interoperability for infection control data.
FHIR enables fast exchange of data thanks to its discrete and independent data elements.
The OMOP CDM supports research to identify and evaluate associations between interventions and outcomes.

supporting_evidence.claim: The HiGHmed Use Case Infection Control group has modelled a set of infection-related data in the openEHR format.
supporting_evidence.quote: The HiGHmed Use Case Infection Control group has modelled a set of infection-related data in the openEHR format.

supporting_evidence.claim: The openEHR information was mapped to the Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) format.
supporting_evidence.quote: we mapped the openEHR information to the Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) format recommended within the initiative.

supporting_evidence.claim: FHIR enables fast exchange of data thanks to the discrete and independent data elements into which information is organized.
supporting_evidence.quote: FHIR enables fast exchange of data thanks to the discrete and independent data elements into which information is organized.

supporting_evidence.claim: The FHIR elements were subsequently mapped to the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM).
supporting_evidence.quote: we subsequently mapped the FHIR elements to the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP CDM).

supporting_evidence.claim: The OMOP data model is designed to support research to identify and evaluate associations between interventions and outcomes caused by these interventions.
supporting_evidence.quote: The OMOP data model is designed to support the conduct of research to identify and evaluate associations between interventions and outcomes caused by these interventions.

supporting_evidence.claim: Mapping across standards allows exploitation of their peculiarities while establishing and/or maintaining interoperability.
supporting_evidence.quote: Mapping across standard allows to exploit their peculiarities while establishing and/or maintaining interoperability.

supporting_evidence.claim: The article provides an overview of the experience in mapping infection control related data across openEHR, FHIR, and OMOP CDM.
supporting_evidence.quote: This article provides an overview of our experience in mapping infection control related data across three different standards openEHR, FHIR and OMOP CDM.

articles.title: Data Integration into OMOP CDM for Heterogeneous Clinical Data Collections via HL7 FHIR Bundles and XSLT.
articles.journal: Studies in health technology and informatics

knowledge.research_objective: Integrate heterogeneous data from a German pulmonary hypertension registry into an OMOP Common Data Model using HL7 FHIR as an intermediate format.
knowledge.etl_architecture: ETL pipeline that extracts data as HL7 FHIR Bundles, then transforms them to OMOP CDM using XSLT.
mapping_techniques: XSLT-based transformation from FHIR Bundle to OMOP CDM
evaluation_methods: Qualitative assessment of transformation completeness (majority of data elements transformed) and runtime feasibility
main_findings: The majority of data elements were successfully transformed to the OMOP CDM
Transformation was achieved in a feasible amount of time

supporting_evidence.claim: The aim was to integrate heterogeneous data from a German pulmonary hypertension registry into an OMOP CDM using HL7 FHIR as an intermediate format.
supporting_evidence.quote: By introducing HL7 FHIR as an intermediate format, our aim was to integrate heterogeneous data from a German pulmonary hypertension registry into an OMOP Common Data Model.

supporting_evidence.claim: Domain experts mapped parameters to standardized terminologies like LOINC and SNOMED-CT.
supporting_evidence.quote: First, domain knowledge experts defined a common parameter set, which was subsequently mapped to standardized terminologies like LOINC or SNOMED-CT.

supporting_evidence.claim: Data was extracted as HL7 FHIR Bundles and transformed to OMOP CDM using XSLT.
supporting_evidence.quote: Data was extracted as HL7 FHIR Bundle to be transformed to OMOP CDM by using XSLT.

supporting_evidence.claim: The majority of data elements were successfully transformed to the OMOP CDM in a feasible time.
supporting_evidence.quote: We successfully transformed the majority of data elements to the OMOP CDM in a feasible time.

articles.title: MENDS-on-FHIR: leveraging the OMOP common data model and FHIR standards for national chronic disease surveillance

knowledge.research_objective: To develop and evaluate an ETL pipeline (MENDS-on-FHIR) that leverages the OMOP CDM and FHIR standards to enable national chronic disease surveillance.
knowledge.etl_architecture: Data are extracted from UCHealth's Epic EHR into a Google Cloud BigQuery relational data mart stored in OMOP CDM V5.3, queried with ANSI‑SQL to produce OMOP‑JSON objects, transformed to FHIR R4 Bundle JSON via the open‑source Whistle JSON‑to‑JSON engine, validated with the HL7 FHIR Validator, and loaded into a FHIR server using a $import call; downstream services retrieve data via $export calls.
mapping_techniques: ANSI‑standard SQL joins to combine OMOP tables and generate OMOP JSON
Whistle functional transformation language for JSON‑to‑JSON conversion from OMOP JSON to FHIR resources
FHIR profile validation using the HL7 FHIR Validator
data_sources: Health Data Compass research data warehouse (clinical, administrative, genomic, external sources)
datasets: MENDS data mart cohort (patients seen at UCHealth)
OMOP CDM V5.3 tables (Person, Death, Condition_Occurrence, etc.)
Synthetic OMOP Condition_Occurrence data used for illustration
evaluation_methods: Conformance validation of generated FHIR resources with the HL7 FHIR Validator configured for FHIR R4 V4.0.1 and US‑Core IG V4.0.0
Logging and inspection of import errors during FHIR $import operations

supporting_evidence.claim: The study addresses the urgent need for rapid access to clinical data for chronic disease surveillance.
supporting_evidence.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the urgent need for rapid access to clinical data from diverse settings to assess emerging risk factors and treatment outcomes... Similarly, chronic disease surveillance registries need timely access to linked clinical, administrative, and social determinants of health data across diverse healthcare settings.

supporting_evidence.claim: The originating data source is an OMOP CDM V5.3 relational database hosted by Health Data Compass.
supporting_evidence.quote: The originating data source is a research data warehouse store in an OMOP CDM Version 5.3 relational database hosted by Health Data Compass (HDC).

supporting_evidence.claim: Clinical data are extracted from UCHealth’s Epic EHR and stored in a GCP BigQuery relational data mart in OMOP CDM V5.3 format.
supporting_evidence.quote: The yellow data flow begins with clinical data extracted from UCHealth’s Epic ® EHR stored in a GCP BigQuery relational data mart in OMOP CDM V5.3 format.

supporting_evidence.claim: ANSI‑standard SQL statements query OMOP CDM V5.3 tables to generate output rows that create FHIR resources.
supporting_evidence.quote: ANSI-standard SQL statements query OMOP CDM V5.3 tables to generate output rows that create FHIR resources.

supporting_evidence.claim: SQL queries produce an "OMOP JSON" object representing rows from OMOP tables.
supporting_evidence.quote: Each SQL statement creates an “OMOP JSON” object ( Figure 1B1 ) consisting of a single key and an array. The JSON key represents the original OMOP table.

supporting_evidence.claim: OMOP JSON is transformed into FHIR R4 Bundle JSON using the Whistle JSON‑to‑JSON transformation engine.
supporting_evidence.quote: OMOP JSON is transformed into FHIR R4 Bundle JSON format using an open-source JSON-to-JSON transformation engine that implements a functional language called Whistle.

supporting_evidence.claim: Whistle transformation files produce FHIR output conformant to FHIR R4 V4.0.1 and US Core IG 4.0.0 specifications.
supporting_evidence.quote: Whistle transformation files create FHIR output that is conformant to FHIR R4 V4.0.1 and US Core IG 4.0.0 specifications.

supporting_evidence.claim: FHIR resources are validated for conformance using the open‑source HL7 FHIR Validator configured for FHIR R4 V4.0.1 and US‑Core IG V4.0.0.
supporting_evidence.quote: FHIR validation tools examine the structure and content of FHIR resources for conformance to FHIR Profiles and IGs using the open-source HL7 FHIR Validator. The validator was configured to use FHIR R4 V4.0.1 and US-Core IG V4.0.0.

supporting_evidence.claim: FHIR Bundle JSON files are uploaded to a FHIR server via a FHIR $import call, with import errors logged for inspection.
supporting_evidence.quote: Each FHIR Bundle JSON file in Figure 1C is uploaded to a FHIR server ... using a FHIR $import call ... Import errors are logged for inspection after all resources are loaded.

supporting_evidence.claim: The ESP server retrieves FHIR resources using a FHIR $export call.
supporting_evidence.quote: The ESP server requests FHIR resources by executing a FHIR $export call to the FHIR server, which launches an asynchronous export process.
